title: Seven All
paragraphs: “You guys, it’s obvious just by looking that the Filolial rides rough. But that’s a problem you can’t avoid if you’re going to be traveling merchants.”
“Whoa—I know that’s true, but… big bro.”
After getting a scolding from Father, the villagers—including Keel—start protesting. Keel is protesting while struggling not to get buried under Luna-chan… he’s quite the tough one, isn’t he?
“That goes for Raphtalia, too. You know that running away now won’t solve anything, right?”
“I know, but…”
“Can’t we make it work with what Big Brother, Sadeena, and Spear-Brother earn? I mean, does it really cost that much?”
When Keel asks this, Father lets out a sigh. Oh dear, is that really what he’s saying? Keel is still just a kid, isn’t he?

“First off, there’s your food expenses, the Filolials’ food expenses, plus the cost of your equipment, living expenses in Zeltoble, and future Class Up fees. Even with the assets I’m managing and everything else, we’re already barely scraping by. To be honest, with just our earnings, who knows when we’ll go bankrupt?”
Isn’t this something Keel and the others are very unlikely to understand? I think that’s a rather unusual way of putting it for Father.

“And another thing. It’s not good to depend on us for everything. You guys know that much, right?　Do you plan to live comfortably off our earnings even after we return to the village? Think of this as a dress rehearsal for rebuilding the village.”
“Ugh…”
The villagers all fell silent. That’s right. I think this is something Father has always said. He’s encouraging us to be self-reliant so we don’t become dependent.

It’s true that I’ve experienced countless loops—including the world Father saved in the first one—so objectively speaking, I’m pretty strong. But this world isn’t so forgiving that I can save it all by myself. Above all, Father is the Shield Hero. It wouldn’t even be possible without allies.
“Let me say this up front: I won’t recognize anyone who lives solely to make money at the Zeltoble Colosseum as self-reliant. It’s obvious that such a lifestyle is bound to collapse eventually.”
“Naofumi-chan says that just fighting and destroying things won’t lead to anything good. It’ll be tough, but let’s all do our best, okay?”

As expected of Father—he speaks wisely. Indeed, those who can do nothing but kill and destroy will meet a fate befitting them. It might be a difficult concept for Keel and the others, living in this era of strife known as “The Waves,” but when the age of peace eventually arrives, they’ll find themselves in trouble. It means that when the era of peace arrives, we must become the kind of people who can create something.

Huh? For some reason, I feel like everyone’s looking at me, but I’m sure it’s just my imagination. I’m The Love Hunter, after all. I work hard every day to win Filo-tan’s heart. It’s true that I show no mercy to my enemies, but that’s all for the sake of peace—to protect everyone. Even I, in a peaceful world, would be cheering at Filo-tan’s concerts day in and day out, and working my tail off just to attend them. I know it’s a future you can’t even imagine right now, but once peace comes, that kind of happy world awaits us. When that world comes to pass, we must not allow a situation to arise where killing is the only option.
“Ugh…”
“Well, I’ll prescribe you some strong motion sickness medicine, so get used to it. Elena seems to be used to riding in carriages—she doesn’t get too sick—so I guess it’ll work out.”
“Boo…”
Lazy Pig… What on earth do you think you’re so proud of for something this trivial! Not getting motion sickness from Filolial’s bumpy ride isn’t something to brag about!
“Keel, it’s okay. Luna will help you so you can handle anything.”
“It’s all Luna-chan’s fault I can’t physically move a muscle right now! Hey—Luna-chan, where are you taking me!?”
Luna-chan struts along, wrapping Keel in feathers and leading him away.
“Someone! Help meeeee! Woof woof!”

Keel is yelping about something, but does he really intend to dismiss Luna-chan’s hard work? Luna-chan is sure to make you exceptionally strong. I’d love to get a special lesson from Filo-tan tooooooo!
“Sigh… After Motoyasu, now I have to take care of these brats. I wonder why I even came to this other world.”

With a sigh like that, Father muttered to himself as he headed off to his business meeting for the day. Just like in the first world, that’s so typical of him. I’ll follow his example and do my best, too!
“Raphtalia, take Elena and Filo with you to go peddling. Motoyasu, just stay put at the Colosseum as usual.”
“Leave it to me!”
Today, too, I’ll use my spear to paint the Colosseum in Filolial colors. After all, in the Colosseum, I’m the Filolial Mask! I’m a guardian of justice fighting for underprivileged children.
“Raphtalia big sister! Let’s go already! Before the guy with the spear gets here!”
“Hold on a sec, Filo, calm down!”
“Boo…”
Filo-tan sure is full of energy. Her Older Sister’s having a hard time keeping up. Trailing behind the two of them, slow as molasses, was the Lazy Pig.
“As for Sadeena… she worked hard yesterday, so she gets free time. The other Filolials and the slaves still have room to level up, so they’ll be hunting and training to overcome motion sickness.”
“Oh my—well then, I’d love to have a drinking party with Naofumi-chan!”
“…I’ll spend a little time with you once the sun goes down, so don’t go causing too much trouble.”
“Okayy~”
“Alright, that’s all for now!”

So, that means I’m off to fight in the Colosseum again today. It’s quite a hassle to go easy on them, but since it’s Father’s order, I guess I have no choice. I’ll vent this pent-up frustration during my free time after the Colosseum is over by heading out to hunt via the portal.

I’ll use my Cloaking Lance—which I use daily—to hide my form, put on the Filolial Mask crafted from Lady Filolial’s feathers, and that’s my change of clothes complete. I’ll go register for the Colosseum. Well, I’ve already been nominated to participate, so I’m just reporting that I’ve arrived.

Apparently, there’s a steady demand for masked fighters. This tournament is called the Masked Colosseum, and since the prize money is high, Father picked it out. According to Father, this is a joint exhibition match between the Light Colosseum and the Colosseum of Darkness. He says that if I perform well here, I’ll be granted permission to compete in the Colosseum of Darkness.

By the way, entry into the Dark Colosseum itself is apparently made possible through the Monster Merchant’s connections, but those without a backer use tournaments like this to get noticed by sponsors and the like. Am I, in a sense, a plant? It seems Sakura-chan is actually Filo-tan! HAHAHA!

At the Colosseum, a lot of people wear iron masks and the like. There’s this vibe that not wearing a helmet or mask is something only fools would do. Well, there are some—like pigs and the like—who don’t wear them because they’re just there for the spectacle, and there are also fighters who are expected to transform into Therianthropes and choose not to wear them because they’d get in the way during the transformation.

I don’t see Older Sister wearing that kind of armor, though. I suppose it’s because her streamlined figure makes it hard to put on? Well, Older Sister possesses skills that even I find astonishing, and her technical growth and adaptability are simply monstrous. She’s such a master that if I take things too leisurely, even I’ll fall behind. It would be rude to lump my Older Sister in with the rest of us greenhorns.

Father strictly forbade the use of Skills. Well, he did say it was okay to use them as long as they looked like regular techniques. That said, I haven’t actually encountered anyone yet who’d require me to use Skills.
I’ve completed my registration and am waiting in the waiting room. After waiting a little while, I was called.
“Now then… Mr. Filolial Mask.”
“Yes, sir.”
Led by an attendant, I’m heading out to the arena again today. That alone sparked a wave of cheers.
“…The solitary bird who loves Filolial and embodies Filolial! Filolial Maaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaskuuuuuuuuuuu!”

A shout so refreshing it’s almost invigorating echoes through the Colosseum. At the same time, I can hear the sound of a bell ringing. Well, I can’t quite become Filolial-sama myself, but as The Love Hunter, I must face my opponent head-on.
Wooooo! I raise both hands and roar, ready to show everyone my victory once again today.
“Guaaaaaa!”

I’m imitating Filo-tan’s cry! The crowd is really getting into it. After all, coming from someone like me, it’s just a poor imitation of an angel’s beautiful voice, but I guess it’s having some effect.
“Hmph. So you’re my first-round opponent. Sorry, but you’re getting knocked out.”
Before the cheers died down, my opponent emerged from the dressing room and stood before me. You should try to blend in a little better with the atmosphere here.

So… what do we have here? A bandana-wearing guy with a butterfly mask. I can tell he’s wearing leather armor that looks like an afterthought. It doesn’t fit him very well, so you can spot it at a glance.

He’s dressed a bit out of place, and he’s a face you don’t usually see among the regulars at the Colosseum. To participate out of the blue with no track record—he must have pulled some strings to get in. He might even be someone with connections to merchants or the like.

Well, this is Zeltoble, the land of merchants and mercenaries. According to Father, it’s a country where almost anything is possible if you pay enough, so there’s no point in wondering about it. As the Filolial Mask, I’ll simply eliminate every enemy that steps onto the stage.
“But… ‘Filolial Mask’… are you making donations to an orphanage or something?”
“I won’t deny it.”

The people from Father’s village are like orphans who suffered from the tsunami, and the building we’re protecting is indeed something like an orphanage. In other words, Filolial Mask fights for the underprivileged.
“Hah… I’m not in the mood for this tear-jerking act. I’ve got my own business to attend to, after all.”
“That’s exactly what I’d say. You’re going to be the one I defeat to advance my career.”
I’m drawing my spear. By the way, what’s this guy’s stage name? The referee’s holding a cheat sheet.

“Unknown for now, but soon the whole world won’t be able to take their eyes off his exploits! The rookie everyone’s watching! Seven- Well, I’ve faced so many guys spouting lines like this that I don’t even need to remember it. I’ll take him down easily today, too.
“‘Boo-boo-boo!’”

It seems like a group of people in the stands—presumably this opponent’s cheering squad—are shouting. But they’re nothing but a bunch of pigs. The fact that he’s got an audience from the start suggests he’s got some potential, but with only pigs in the crowd, you can tell how limited that potential is.
“And nowwwwwwwwwwwwwww! Let’s biiiiiiiiiiiiiggin’!”

The Last Judgment’s voice rings out simultaneously with the bell signaling the start of the match. Seven-All—or whatever his name is—is wielding what looks like a sword. From the looks of it, it seems to be quite a fine weapon. Judging by its shape, I’d say it’s a sword of dragon origin. It might be quite difficult to get one of those even in this country.
“Well, since it’s the first match… drop dead right away.”
Seven-All crouched low and charged straight at me. Hmm… that’s quite the speed and lunge. Among those I’ve fought in the Colosseum so far, his speed ranks among the top few.
“Whoa!”

However, everything about him—from his experience to his movements—is still quite immature. His movements are so predictably linear that I can’t help but be taken aback. That might work against monsters or bandits of that caliber, but with skills like that, he won’t even be able to land a hit on me.
“What!? You’re keeping up with my movements—”
“You’re too slow.”
I swoop around behind him, wedge the tip of my spear into a gap in his leather armor, and slam him into the ground with a spinning motion.

Ah, combined with his own momentum, I must’ve slammed him down with quite a bit of force. With a thud that made the ground rumble, the opponent sank into the ground. Hmm, if I trust my instincts, he still seems able to move. Did I go easy on him? Just to be safe, I slammed him down one more time.

I quickly yanked the spearhead out and tossed it aside. He’s twitching a bit, but he’s not moving. What a truly pathetic sight. The Last Judgment came over immediately and began checking on the opponent. Then he crossed his arms.
“Seven All—the match is deemed unfit to continue! The winner! Filolial Maaaaaaaskkkkkkkkkk!”
Without a moment’s delay, here comes the victory pose. The pose of the raging Lord Filolial!
“It’s Guaaaaaaaaaaa!”
“Wooooohhhhhhh!”
The Filolial Mask is the best! Well, it’s only the first round, after all. Things like this happen.
“‘Bubububu!? Bub! Bubububu!’”
Some pig who was cheering for “Seven All” or whatever is yelling, but I don’t care. This is the Colosseum. The victor claims glory, and the loser falls.

Since the next match is coming up, Seven All was carried off on a stretcher. I’m heading back to the dressing room to take a break, too. This downtime is a bit of a hassle, but since it pays, I guess I have to put up with it.

Plus, Father said that if I win this tournament, I’ll be allowed to buy an extra Filolial as a reward. That really gets me fired up. By the way, the last time I asked for an accessory made from Filolial’s feathers as a reward, I got too carried away and ended up getting scolded by Father.
Not long after that, the next match began, and it was time for my match again. The matches are moving along pretty quickly.
Anyway, I won the championship without much trouble.
“It’s Kueeeeeee!” Number of heroines in Seven All: -2
